templates.why_chosen: Extreme size asymmetry: a small CPU/Controller pair broadcasts instructions into a large 3D grid of homogeneous vertex/edge PUs, with an inside dashed legend for the per-PU instruction/state/response cycle and a time axis beside the grid.
templates.what_to_learn: Let the two sides be wildly unequal in size when the paper's point is scale: a tiny controller box against a wall of identical device units, connected by fan-out (broadcast) and fan-in (convergecast) arrows, with a small dashed legend for the repeating per-unit cycle placed beside the small side.

templates.why_chosen: An unusual phase variant: instead of a horizontal time arrow, five measurement-round labels (t=1us to t=5us) run along the receding depth of a 3D isometric grid of vertex/edge PUs, replacing dashed phase columns with perspective.
templates.what_to_learn: A time axis does not have to run left-to-right along the bottom: this figure stacks its five measurement rounds into the depth of a 3D grid instead, which is a legitimate but riskier alternative to labeled vertical phase rules, since perspective compresses the later time steps.

templates.why_chosen: A grid-as-floorplan variant: identical vertex-PU and edge-PU cells tile a 3D block like a systolic array, with the CPU/Controller drawn off to the side as the control block rather than inside the compute grid.
templates.what_to_learn: Treat a homogeneous processing-unit array (vertex/edge PUs here) like a systolic array for floorplan purposes: tile it as one repeated grid, keep the controller as a separate small block feeding it from outside, and use fan-out/fan-in arrows only where the broadcast and convergecast genuinely cross the grid boundary.
